name: IRONLIMB Fortress MK-IV Combat Leg Pair
product_name: Ironlimb Fortress MK-IV Combat Leg Pair
description:
The Fortress MK-IV is a bilateral combat leg system built from ballistic-grade hardened steel alloy with layered polymer impact-absorption struts running through the tibia and femur analogs. Knee joints are triple-redundant hydraulic with magnetic boot interface plates rated for 800kg attachment force, allowing the user to lock to ferromagnetic surfaces in zero-G or high-turbulence environments. A hydraulic shock buffer in each heel absorbs fall impact up to 6 meters without joint damage.

The MK-IV is standard issue in several GLMZ private security contractors and sees heavy use among ex-military personnel who kept their service hardware after discharge. It carries the aesthetic charm of a shipping container — flat matte black, exposed bolt heads, no decorative flourishes — and its users wear that ugliness as a point of pride.
installation_requirements: Restricted license required, military or licensed combat clinic installation, full bilateral neural mapping, 72-hour monitored recovery
rejection_risk: Moderate — steel alloy mass requires extended neural adaptation period, joint inflammation common in first month
maintenance: Hydraulic fluid replacement every 6 months, magnetic boot plate recalibration quarterly, impact buffer inspection after any fall exceeding 4 meters

cultural_context: The Fortress MK-IV has an unofficial motto in private security circles: 'If you can see the welds, you know it works.' Ironlimb makes no effort to conceal the industrial manufacturing process, and veterans who chose the MK-IV over prettier options treat that visible construction as a statement of practical values over vanity.

story_hooks: A decommissioned MK-IV pair surfaces at a black market auction with classified military firmware still active — whoever wore them last left behind encrypted movement logs that someone powerful wants deleted.
The magnetic boot interface is being exploited by a crew that uses MK-IV wearers as living anchors on the exterior of moving cargo barges during heists.
A Fortress user's hydraulic fluid has been adulterated with a chemical that causes catastrophic joint failure under stress — someone is targeting ex-military veterans specifically.
